question: What is the maximum height above the ground at which I can fly a drone in the open category?
reference_answer: 120 metres from the closest point of the surface of the earth (Article 4(1)(e)). Part A of the Annex (UAS.OPEN.010) adds exceptions: up to 15 m above an artificial obstacle taller than 105 m at the request of the entity responsible for it, and unmanned sailplanes under 10 kg.

question: What is the minimum age to operate a drone as a remote pilot in the open category?
reference_answer: 16 years (Article 9(1)). No minimum age applies in subcategory A1 with a class C0 toy drone, for privately built UAS under 250 g, or under the direct supervision of a qualifying remote pilot. Member States may lower the age by up to 4 years in the open category, and such pilots may then only fly in that Member State.

question: In subcategory A2, how close can I fly to uninvolved people, and can that distance be reduced?
reference_answer: At least 30 m horizontally from uninvolved persons. The remote pilot may reduce it to a minimum of 5 m when the aircraft has an active low-speed mode function, after evaluating the weather conditions, the performance of the aircraft and the segregation of the overflown area (UAS.OPEN.030(1)).

question: In subcategory A3, how far from residential, commercial, industrial or recreational areas must I fly?
reference_answer: At a safe horizontal distance of at least 150 metres from residential, commercial, industrial or recreational areas (UAS.OPEN.040(2)).

question: Which unmanned aircraft may be flown in subcategory A1?
reference_answer: Privately built UAS under 250 g and under 19 m/s; legacy aircraft under 250 g covered by Article 20(a); class C0 aircraft; and class C1 aircraft, which must be operated with an active and updated direct remote identification system and geo-awareness function (UAS.OPEN.020(5)).

question: How long is a certificate of remote pilot competency valid, and how is it revalidated?
reference_answer: Five years. Within its validity it is revalidated by demonstrating the competencies (the exam) or by completing refresher training given by the competent authority or a designated entity. Once expired, it can only be revalidated by demonstrating the competencies again (UAS.OPEN.070).

question: How many questions does the online theoretical exam for a C1 drone in subcategory A1 have, and what score do I need to pass?
reference_answer: 40 multiple-choice questions, and at least 75% of the overall marks (UAS.OPEN.020(4)(b)).

question: Which drone operators have to register themselves when flying in the open category?
reference_answer: Operators of an aircraft with a take-off mass of 250 g or more, or one that can transfer more than 80 joules of kinetic energy to a human on impact, or one equipped with a sensor able to capture personal data (unless it complies with the toy directive 2009/48/EC). In the specific category operators must register for an aircraft of any mass (Article 14(5)).

question: What must an operational declaration for a standard scenario contain?
reference_answer: Administrative information about the UAS operator; a statement that the operation satisfies the operational requirements and a standard scenario of Appendix 1; the operator's commitment to apply the relevant mitigation measures (operation instructions, aircraft design, competency of personnel); and confirmation that appropriate insurance cover will be in place for every flight, if required by Union or national law (UAS.SPEC.020(2)).

question: When do I need an operational authorisation in the specific category, and who grants it?
reference_answer: When one of the requirements of Article 4 or Part A of the Annex (open category) is not met. The operator applies to the competent authority of the Member State where it is registered, with a risk assessment and adequate mitigating measures (Article 5(1)-(2)); for operations that fit a standard scenario a declaration is enough (Article 5(5)).

question: What are the main technical requirements of a class C0 drone?
reference_answer: Take-off mass below 250 g including payload; maximum speed in level flight of 19 m/s; maximum attainable height above the take-off point limited to 120 m; exclusively electrically powered; and, if it has a follow-me mode, it stays within 50 m of the remote pilot (Part 1).

question: What maximum take-off mass does a class C2 drone have, and what speed function must it offer?
reference_answer: Take-off mass below 4 kg including payload (point 1). Unless it is a fixed-wing aircraft it must have a low-speed mode, selectable by the remote pilot, limiting ground speed to no more than 3 m/s (point 9).

question: How long must manufacturers keep the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity of a drone?
reference_answer: For 10 years after the product has been placed on the market (Article 6(3)).

question: Which U-space services are mandatory for all drone operations in U-space airspace?
reference_answer: The network identification service, the geo-awareness service, the UAS flight authorisation service and the traffic information service (Article 3(2)). Member States may also require the weather information and conformance monitoring services (Article 3(3)).

question: Within what time limit must an aviation occurrence be reported under mandatory reporting?
reference_answer: Within 72 hours of becoming aware of the occurrence, unless exceptional circumstances prevent it (Article 4(7)).

question: Does the occurrence reporting regulation apply to an accident with a small drone that needs no certificate or declaration?
reference_answer: No, unless the occurrence resulted in a fatal or serious injury to a person or involved aircraft other than unmanned aircraft (Article 3(2)). Member States may decide to apply the regulation more widely.

question: I plan to fly a class C2 drone in subcategory A2. What is the maximum take-off mass of a C2 drone and what horizontal distance must I keep from uninvolved people?
reference_answer: A class C2 drone has a take-off mass below 4 kg including payload (Reg. 2019/945, Part 3 point 1). In A2 the remote pilot keeps at least 30 m horizontally from uninvolved persons, reducible to a minimum of 5 m with an active low-speed mode after evaluating weather, aircraft performance and segregation (Reg. 2019/947, UAS.OPEN.030(1)).

question: Which kinds of drone may be flown in subcategory A3, and what take-off mass limit does a class C3 drone have?
reference_answer: A3 allows privately built UAS under 25 kg, legacy aircraft under 25 kg (Article 20(b)), class C2 and C3 aircraft operated with active and updated direct remote identification and geo-awareness, and class C4 aircraft (UAS.OPEN.040(4)). A class C3 aircraft has a take-off mass below 25 kg including payload and a maximum characteristic dimension below 3 m (Reg. 2019/945, Part 4 point 1).

question: To fly a C1 drone in subcategory A1, what remote identification is required, and what data does a direct remote identification broadcast?
reference_answer: A C1 drone in A1 must be operated with an active and updated direct remote identification system and geo-awareness function (UAS.OPEN.020(5)(d)). Direct remote identification broadcasts in real time the operator registration number and verification code, the aircraft's unique serial number, time stamp, position and height, route course and ground speed, the position of the remote pilot (or take-off point) and the emergency status (Reg. 2019/945, Part 2 point 12).

question: As a UAS operator, which regulation governs how I report a safety-related occurrence, and what is the time limit for mandatory reports?
reference_answer: Article 19(2) of Reg. 2019/947 requires each UAS operator to report safety-related occurrences to the competent authority in compliance with Regulation (EU) No 376/2014. Under Article 4(7) of that regulation, mandatory reports are made within 72 hours of becoming aware of the occurrence, unless exceptional circumstances prevent it.

question: In U-space airspace, which services must be used, and what must the UAS operator do before each flight?
reference_answer: All operations are subject to the network identification, geo-awareness, UAS flight authorisation and traffic information services (Article 3(2)), plus any additional services the Member State requires. Before each flight the operator submits a UAS flight authorisation request to its U-space service provider and, when ready to start, requests activation; it may start once activation is confirmed (Article 6(4)-(5)).

question: Does the U-space regulation apply to a class C0 drone flown in subcategory A1, and what are the main limits of class C0?
reference_answer: No: Reg. 2021/664 does not apply to subcategory A1 operations with an aircraft marked as class C0 (Article 1(3)(b)). Class C0 means a take-off mass below 250 g, a maximum speed of 19 m/s in level flight and a maximum attainable height of 120 m above the take-off point (Reg. 2019/945, Part 1).

question: Which authority grants an operational authorisation in the specific category, and how long does it last?
reference_answer: The competent authority of the Member State where the operator is registered (Article 5(1)). The authority specifies the duration in the authorisation itself, and it remains valid as long as the operator stays compliant with the regulation and the conditions of the authorisation (UAS.SPEC.080).

question: What height limit applies to a class C3 drone, and what height limit applies to open-category operations in general?
reference_answer: A class C3 aircraft has a maximum attainable height of 120 m above the take-off point or a system limiting height to 120 m or to a value the remote pilot selects (Reg. 2019/945, Part 4 point 2). Open-category operations keep the aircraft within 120 m of the closest point of the surface of the earth (Reg. 2019/947, Article 4(1)(e)).

question: What must an open-category operator check about a drone's class label, and how big must the label be?
reference_answer: For aircraft of classes C0 to C4 the operator must ensure the aircraft is accompanied by the EU declaration of conformity with the reference to its class and that the class identification label is affixed to it (UAS.OPEN.050(6)). The label must be at least 5 mm high and affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly (Reg. 2019/945, Article 16(2)).

question: Which Spanish authority is responsible for running the national register of drone operators?
reference_answer: NOT COVERED: the documents do not name the Spanish authority. Reg. 2019/947 Article 14(1) only says each Member State must establish and maintain registration systems.

question: Which class label does the DJI Mini 4 Pro carry?
reference_answer: NOT COVERED: the documents define the classes C0 to C6 but never mention specific drone models.

question: How many euros is the fine in Spain for flying a drone over a crowd of people?
reference_answer: NOT COVERED: no fine amounts appear in the documents. They only say the remote pilot must not fly over assemblies of people in the open category (Reg. 2019/947 Article 4(1)(c)).

question: What is the minimum insurance cover, in euros, that a drone operator must have?
reference_answer: NOT COVERED: the documents give no insurance amount; Reg. 2019/947 only mentions insurance where required by Union or national law (for example Article 14(2)(d)).

question: How much does the A2 certificate of competency exam cost?
reference_answer: NOT COVERED: exam fees are not mentioned; the documents only describe the exam content and the 75% pass mark (UAS.OPEN.030(2)).

question: Where can I download the official map of UAS geographical zones for Italy?
reference_answer: NOT COVERED: the documents do not say where any country publishes its zones; Reg. 2019/947 Article 15(3) only requires Member States to make them public in a common unique digital format.

question: How many drone operators are registered in the European Union?
reference_answer: NOT COVERED: the documents contain no registration statistics.

question: What is the maximum fine under Regulation 376/2014 for failing to report an occurrence?
reference_answer: NOT COVERED: Article 21 leaves penalties to the Member States, which must make them effective, proportionate and dissuasive; the regulation states no amounts.

question: Which airspace in Germany has been designated as U-space airspace?
reference_answer: NOT COVERED: the documents do not list designated U-space airspaces; Reg. 2021/664 Article 3 leaves the designation to each Member State.

question: When flying at night in the open category, what must the remote pilot make sure of on the drone?
reference_answer: The remote pilot must ensure that a green flashing light on the unmanned aircraft is activated (UAS.OPEN.060, responsibilities of the remote pilot, point (g)).

question: In subcategory A1, up to what distance from the remote pilot may a drone fly in follow-me mode?
reference_answer: Up to 50 metres from the remote pilot while the follow-me mode is active; this is a derogation from the rule that the drone must be kept in VLOS (UAS.OPEN.020(3), derogating from Article 4(1)(d)).

question: In standard scenario STS-02, how far from the remote pilot may the drone fly if no airspace observer is used?
reference_answer: No further than 1 km from the remote pilot, and the drone must follow a pre-programmed trajectory whenever it is not in VLOS of the remote pilot (UAS.STS-02.020(5)).

question: What does 'assemblies of people' mean in the drone regulation?
reference_answer: Gatherings where persons are unable to move away due to the density of the people present (Article 2(3)).

question: I fly a class C1 drone at night in the open category: what light must the drone have, and what must I do as remote pilot?
reference_answer: A class C1 drone must have at least one green flashing light for conspicuity at night, so that a person on the ground can tell it from a manned aircraft (Reg. 2019/945, Part 2). As remote pilot I must make sure that this green flashing light is activated when operating at night (Reg. 2019/947, UAS.OPEN.060, point (g)).

question: For standard scenario STS-01, which drone class is required and what low-speed mode must it offer?
reference_answer: A drone marked as class C5 (UAS.STS-01.020(f)). Unless it is tethered, a class C5 drone must have a low-speed mode selectable by the remote pilot that limits the ground speed to not more than 5 m/s (Reg. 2019/945, Part 16, point (4)); STS-01 itself requires a ground speed below 5 m/s for untethered aircraft (UAS.STS-01.020(d)).

question: Who may set a different minimum age for pilots in a model aircraft club, and what does the club need from the authority?
reference_answer: Member States may define a different minimum age for remote pilots operating in the framework of model aircraft clubs or associations, in the authorisation issued under Article 16 (Article 9(5)). The club must ask the competent authority, which may issue an authorisation that specifies the conditions of the operations and is limited to the territory of the Member State that issued it (Article 16(1) and (3)).

question: What minimum flight time (battery endurance) must a C1 drone have?
reference_answer: NOT COVERED: the class C1 requirements in Reg. 2019/945 (Part 2) set limits such as mass and a maximum speed of 19 m/s, but no minimum flight time or endurance.

question: What is the minimum distance from an airport that I must keep when flying a drone in Spain?
reference_answer: NOT COVERED: the documents give no distances from airports; Reg. 2019/947 Article 15 only requires Member States to define UAS geographical zones and make them public.

question: How much does it cost to register as a UAS operator?
reference_answer: NOT COVERED: Reg. 2019/947 Article 14 regulates the registration of UAS operators but states no fees.

question: How many hours of practical flight training do I need before taking the A2 exam?
reference_answer: NOT COVERED: UAS.OPEN.030 requires a self-practical training in the operating conditions of subcategory A3 and a declaration that it was completed, but sets no number of hours.
